# Workshop Dust Collection

## Overview

The shop is a single garage bay, about 18 square metres, and wood dust was coating every surface before I set up extraction. Fine particulates are the real problem; they hang around for hours and end up in my lungs. I run a 1 hp blower with a cyclone separator ahead of it, so most of the debris drops out before it reaches the filter. Coarse shavings fall into a drum and only the lightest fraction goes on to the pleated element. It is a modest setup but it changed how the room feels after an afternoon of work. It is not a full shop system, but it catches the bulk of the problem.

## Ducting

The main run is 100 mm PVC, stepped down to 50 mm flex at the smaller equipment. Blast gates sit at every branch so I only pull from the tool in use. Long sweeps instead of sharp elbows maintain the flow. The cyclone separator sits on a 60 litre drum, which I empty when it is two-thirds full. Every tool has a dedicated port within a metre so the hose does not kink. Extraction at each tool matters more than raw blower size; a short hose on the right port beats a big unit with long runs. I numbered the gates and wrote the order on the wall, because opening the wrong one starves the tool in use.

## Maintenance

I shake the filter cartridge monthly and tap it outside; a clogged pleated element kills suction fast. The drum gets emptied weekly during heavy work. Blast gates get a drop of silicone on the slide twice a year. I check the duct joints each season for leaks, since a loose collar lets fine particles escape back into the room. The blower bearings were noisy at 18 months, so I replaced them and now listen for rumble at startup. A spare cartridge on the shelf saves a wasted weekend.
